findings.title: Denial cache can mask newly granted permissions until TTL expiry
findings.body: The new permDenialCache stores a 'denied' result for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) keyed by namespace/user/action/name/parent. If a user is denied access and then permissions change (e.g. they are granted access, or create the resource) within that 30s window, the Check() call will short-circuit to a cached denial at line 117-121 without re-querying the DB, returning Allowed=false even though the user now has access. This directly undermines the stated goal of the PR (allowing users to access resources they just created), since any earlier failed check for the same name/action will keep denying access for up to 30 seconds afterward.

findings.title: Redundant lookups when cached permissions exist but check fails
findings.body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns permissions but checkPermission(ctx, cachedPerms, checkReq) returns false (stale/incomplete cache), the code falls through to call getIdentityPermissions, which for TypeUser/TypeServiceAccount calls GetUserIdentifiers (and getUserBasicRole/getUserTeams) again. GetUserIdentifiers was already resolved inside getCachedIdentityPermissions just moments earlier, so the same cache lookups/sql queries for identifiers are effectively repeated. Not incorrect, but adds avoidable overhead on every cache-miss request.

findings.title: Render service identity never benefits from permission caching
findings.body: getCachedIdentityPermissions always returns cache.ErrNotFound for types.TypeRenderService (line 353-355), forcing getIdentityPermissions -> getRendererPermissions to be computed on every single Check/List call for renderer identities, even though the result is static and cheap to cache. While getRendererPermissions is cheap, this inconsistency with other identity types means the renderer path bypasses the whole caching/denial mechanism introduced in this PR.

findings.title: In-proc authz client caching disabled entirely
findings.body: ProvideAuthZClient now passes `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})` for the in-proc client instead of a real cache (previously a `cache.NewLocalCache` was used). This means every Check/List call made in-proc now always crosses the gRPC channel without any client-side caching, relying solely on the server-side permission cache added in rbac/service.go. If the server-side cache has a cache miss or needs singleflight dedup under load, this adds overhead for every single authorization check in-proc that was previously avoided by the client cache; the PR description claims this is intentional for resolving stale-cache resource-creation issues, but it removes a layer of caching for all other read-heavy authz checks that aren't related to freshly-created resources.
